Theme

Travel & transport · Town, shops & places

bus stop noun

also stop, tram stop

* our formation

* (our own formation) statiō, statiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a stopping place: a bus stop

Our use, as in the lexicon’s statiō ferriviāria (train station): classically a place where one stands or waits (Lewis & Short; stationēs, public places where people sit about, Plin. Ep. 1.13.2). In full, statiō autoraedārum longārum, after Traupman’s hōrārium autoraedārum longārum (bus timetable, p. 218). No reference work has a word for a bus stop.

Examples

  • Ad statiōnem currāmus; autoraeda longa venit!

    Let’s run to the bus stop; the bus is coming!composed

See also bus, schedule, train station.

SourcesLewis & Short: statio

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 218, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
